source_refs.note: Meta Directing (Deactivating) Groups: a main subheading of 20.4 Orientation in Electrophilic Substitution Reactions, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 68-69.

blocks.text: Group that makes the ring less reactive than benzene, and directs the incoming electrophile to attack on meta position only is called as-meta director. Such groups are mostly electron-withdrawing groups, that destabilize the arenium intermediate. These substituents direct the reaction to give primarily the “meta” (1,3) product.

blocks.alt: Nitrobenzene, with Cl2 over the arrow and AlCl3 under it, gives meta-chloronitrobenzene, the Cl on the carbon meta to NO2.
blocks.caption: Chlorination of nitrobenzene (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 69).

blocks.text: Major product formed in this case is meta substituted. Examples of meta– directors include -CN, C=O, -NO₂, -CO₂-. Nitrobenzene contains a meta directing group (-NO₂), its chlorination occurs at the meta position.
